newsitem.title: USA: Judge screens jury prospects in Florida tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge screens jury prospects in Florida tobacco trial.

text.p: A Florida judge presiding over the state's $1 billion lawsuit against the tobacco industry Tuesday dismissed two prospective jurors who said their knowledge of the case made it impossible for them to be objective.

Palm Beach Circuit Judge Harold Cohen dismissed the two jurors and nine others with financial problems in the second day of searching for at least 120 Palm Beach County residents who might be suitable jury candidates for a trial that could last until January.
"We are doing a lot better than I had anticipated," Cohen said, explaining he had approved 23 out of 50 people interviewed.
Florida's lawsuit, seeking to recover the Medicaid costs of treating people with smoking-related illnesses, is the first of 40 filed by state attorneys general to go to trial.
Cohen will seat six jurors and nine alternates for the trial. Testimony is expected to begin in early September.
